summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Tom Allen had skipped to Windsor, Ontario, to avoid prosecution in Kentucky over the Goss-Allen fight, after giving $1,000 bail in Chicago and failing to appear.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Sunday Morning, November 12, 1876, page 7.

facts.fact: Allen was arrested in Chicago at the instance of Kentucky officers for violating Kentucky statutes in the Goss-Allen fight, and gave $1,000 bail to appear before Justice Scully, with Mike McDonald as bondsman
Allen failed to appear and skipped out for Windsor, Ontario, to avoid prosecution in Kentucky
Billy Harrison, advance agent for Mace and Allen, was on his way to California to prepare exhibitions by the two pugilists; Mace had also gone west

notes: Mentions his trial was set for the 20th of November 1876.
